- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a steep drop — adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with low sentiment, reduce forecast slope to avoid mean reversion bias.
- If model forecasts a sharp drop after a recent peak, check sentiment for reversal — if sentiment turns positive, reduce downward forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature sell-off.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.33, 1.00), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing direction, not just price momentum.
